name: Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd
tagline: Confirmed as an independently listed large-cap (NSE: VAML, BSE: 544780) following Vedanta Ltd's May-June 2026 four-way demerger - India's largest aluminium/alumina producer with a named capacity-doubling plan, but currently posting negative TTM earnings against an extremely rich ~34x P/B.
business_overview: Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd (VAML) is India's largest aluminium and alumina producer and the world's third-largest aluminium producer ex-China, operating the world's largest single-location aluminium smelter (Jharsuguda, Odisha). It began independent trading on NSE/BSE on 15 June 2026 after the demerger of Vedanta Ltd into four listed entities (Aluminium, Oil & Gas, Power, Iron & Steel), effective 1 May 2026. This resolves the state.json uncertainty: 'Vedanta Aluminium' is NOT merely an internal division - it is now a distinct, confirmed listed entity (VAML).

fundamentals_narrative: VAML is unambiguously a scale leader - the world's largest single-location smelter and India's #1 aluminium/alumina producer - and it does carry a specific, named structural inflection (the 3 MTPA -> 6 MTPA capacity doubling). But the numbers available this soon after the demerger are hard to read as an entry case: TTM earnings are negative (likely a mix of global aluminium-price cyclicality and finance costs from the debt allocated in the demerger), and the ~34x P/B is a steep premium to peers for a business with ~0% current ROE/ROCE. Some of this distortion is mechanical (a freshly carved-out equity base, thin post-listing history), but there is not enough here to call it undervalued.
